extracted.intended_audience: new journalists; journalism, media and mass communication students; scholars of journalistic theory and practice
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and practical guidance on constructive journalism: what it means, its underlying principles, historical precedents, and how it is practiced in newsrooms. Intended to guide journalists, students, and scholars in applying constructive approaches to reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles of constructive journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets out the guiding principles for a journalism that aims to do more than simply inform about problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book asks what constructive journalism means, what the underlying principles are, how it is practiced, and in what ways it differs from other types of journalism; draws on studies of practitioners and researchers to define these principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practices of constructive journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical methods and newsroom practices for implementing constructive journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The volume discusses how constructive journalism is practiced, provides precedents and examples, and aims to guide new journalists and students in applying these practices (chapter: 'Practices of constructive journalism').

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim beyond problem-reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive journalism 'aims to do more than simply inform about problems.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicates a reporting approach that goes beyond describing problems—suggesting emphasis on context, solutions, and constructive framing (asserted as a defining goal in the book description).
